question: If perceptibility is not the objects' property, what is our position?
premises: the manifest object unites with awareness in that grasp
counter to it stands this very perceptibility
here we state: suppose perceptibility is no object-property
inference: The siddhanta opens: perceptibility is the union-event, to be spelled out.
uncertainties: praty esa (counter/answer) may personify the reply; verse breaks mid-argument
plain_english: The manifest object unites with it — counter to that stands this very perceptibility. Here we say: if perceptibility is no property of objects...
